- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak values, especially in early 30d window.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7d high), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below prior high or adjust downward by 1–3% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate downward moves — reduce forecast lows by 1–2% in early 30d, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mid-range values if sentiment shows no clear direction.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags — adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift, especially if price is still trending down.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a false recovery — reduce forecast mid-range by 1–2% if sentiment remains negative for 3+ days.
- Model tends to overestimate short-term volatility in sentiment-driven markets — smooth 30d forecast by reducing standard deviation by 10–20% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
